practical.title: Calibrated microscopy
practical.subtitle: Measure human cells
practical.objective: Calibrate the eyepiece scale and measure a model epithelial cell in micrometres.
practical.principle: Magnification enlarges an image. Calibration converts eyepiece divisions into a real specimen size; it must be repeated when the objective changes.

steps.title: Prepare the slide
steps.detail: Place the prepared epithelial slide on the stage and begin with the low-power objective.

steps.title: Calibrate the scale
steps.detail: Align the graticule with the stage micrometer. Establish micrometres per eyepiece division.

steps.title: Focus and measure
steps.detail: Select the objective, focus the cell boundary and read the calibrated scale across the cell.

steps.title: Record and evaluate
steps.detail: Record the size and unit. Explain why a larger image does not mean a larger cell.

practical.variable: Change objective magnification; observe image size and calibrated cell size.
practical.controls: Use the same cell and the same eyepiece. Recalibrate for each objective.
practical.caution: Handle glass slides carefully and keep the objective clear of the coverslip.
practical.simLimit: The rendered cell is an illustrative model; a real specimen has irregular boundaries and focusing uncertainty.

question.prompt: An objective is changed from 10× to 40×. What should happen to the calculated size of the same cell?
options: It stays approximately the same after recalibration.
question.explanation: The image grows, but the physical cell does not. The new calibration compensates for the changed magnification.

status: Prepare the slide complete. Align the graticule with the stage micrometer. Establish micrometres per eyepiece division.
